title: Rio-Santos Coast Road
slogan: The BR-101 along the Serra do Mar: Atlantic forest falling into the sea, coves on one side and granite on the other.

scenicChapters.title: Rio-Santos Highway
scenicChapters.narrative: Expect company on a summer weekend. Early is better than fast. For 28 km this is Rio-Santos Highway, a road with a name of its own and a reason for it.

title: Campos do Jordão Climb
slogan: Up the Mantiqueira to the highest town in Brazil: araucaria pine, cold nights and a road that climbs sixteen hundred metres.

waypoints.name: Campos do Jordão
waypoints.advice: 61 km in you reach Campos do Jordão. The road climbs 1038 m over the 30 km before it, steadily. Reckon on about 7 °C colder than the valley, and more in the wind. Nothing on this route is higher. Next is São Bento do Sapucaí, 31 km on and mostly downhill.

waypoints.advice: São Bento do Sapucaí closes the day. You lose 848 m on the way down to it, steadily.

scenicChapters.narrative: For 15 km this is Campos do Jordão Climb, a road with a name of its own and a reason for it. Expect company on a summer weekend. Early is better than fast.

scenicChapters.title: Campos do Jordão Climb
scenicChapters.narrative: A steady rhythm suits this better than bursts. The height arrives whether you hurry or not. The ground tilts up and stays tilted for 48 km. 1038 m of it, taken steadily rather than in one wall.

scenicChapters.title: Campos do Jordão Climb
scenicChapters.narrative: 30 km that neither climbs nor drops much. The road settles into the ground rather than fighting it — this is where a day makes up time without anyone trying. Third and fourth, and very little else.

title: Serra da Mantiqueira Ridge
slogan: The ridge road between São Paulo and Minas: coffee on the slopes, cloud in the mornings and very little traffic once you are up.
